25 years ago today, Mulholland Drive premiered. 

David Lynch's Mulholland Drive (2001) began as an $8 million television pilot for ABC before being dropped and later transformed into a feature film. ABC executives famously rejected the original 1999 television pilot for being too bizarre and open-ended. David Lynch returned in 2000 with funding from StudioCanal (via French producers Pierre Edelman and Alain Sarde) to add roughly 45 to 50 minutes of new material, including the darker reality-based final act. The completed film earned Lynch the Best Director award at the Cannes Film Festival alongside an Academy Award nomination, and was voted the greatest film of the 21st century in a major BBC Culture Poll.
